en.title: Buying property in Cyprus: the contract, the fees and the title deed
en.lede: A contract, an acquisition permit and a title deed are three documents. This is the order a buyer meets them in, and the charges that are not the price on the brochure.
en.desc: The purchase sequence in Cyprus: title checks, the contract, Land Registry lodging, transfer fees and VAT.
en.alt: A house in Ayia Marina Chrysochous, in the Paphos district

faq.q: Is a signed contract the same as ownership?
faq.a: No. Title is the Land Registry record after transfer. Lodging the contract protects the right to insist on that transfer. It does not complete it.

The Ministry of Interior says citizens of non-EU states need permission before they acquire property, on form COMM 145. EU and EEA citizens are treated differently. Read the ministry’s current page rather than a 2007 English consolidation.
PwC’s 2026 booklet states 3 percent, then 5 percent, then 8 percent, with no fee when VAT applies and a 50 percent reduction when it does not. The Land Registry charges the fee. Confirm it there.

faq.q: Does stamp duty still apply in 2026?
faq.a: Stamp duty was part of the 2026 reform. Ask the Tax Department whether a sale contract signed now still has to be stamped before you pay a scale from an older guide.

faq.q: Does the purchase make me tax resident or give me a permit?
faq.a: No. Tax residence is a day-count and, for the 60-day rule, an activity test. A residence permit is a separate application, including the €300,000 investment route where that is the plan.

en.body:
A signed contract is not a title deed, and a title deed is not permission for a non-EU buyer to acquire the property. Those are three different documents. This guide is the sequence a buyer actually walks: the search, the checks, the contract, the money that is not the price, and the moment the Land Registry records the new owner. It is not a valuation and not a promise that a particular project is a sound purchase.

## Before any deposit

See the property, and see the Land Registry record of it. The Department of Lands and Surveys keeps the title. Its portal is [portal.dls.moi.gov.cy](https://portal.dls.moi.gov.cy/). A printout from an agent is a start. The search is the record.

Ask, in writing, for four things.

- The title number, and whether there is a separate title for this unit or only a mother title still in the developer’s name.
- The encumbrances: mortgages, memos and other charges, and any right of way or other burden the search shows.
- The planning position: the permit for what was built, and whether the unit matches it.
- Who is selling. A company seller needs a company search as well as a title search. An individual seller needs to be the person named on the title, or to hold a power that actually allows the sale.

A lawyer who acts for the buyer, not for the seller, is the usual way those questions get asked. The fee is a matter for that lawyer. This page does not invent one. Notes on named developments, where the site has reported what the developer publishes, are collected on the [guides hub](/en/guides/).

{{figure:strovolos-house}}

## The contract

The contract of sale is the document that sets the price, the deadline, what is included, and what happens if a separate title is not out yet. Read the clauses on delivery, on defects, and on who pays if a charge has to be cleared before transfer. A reservation form with a card payment is not that contract.

### Stamp duty

Stamp duty on instruments was part of the 2026 tax reform. Older guides still quote a scale of nil, then 0.15 percent, then 0.20 percent, with a cap. Do not pay from a 2024 printout. Ask the Tax Department whether a sale contract signed now has to be stamped, and for how much, before the Land Registry will accept it. The [MyCyTax stamp-duty calculator](https://mycytax.com/calculators/stamp-duty/) is a way to test a figure against the scale that calculator currently uses. It is not the assessment.

### Lodging the contract at the Land Registry

A buyer who wants the contract to be enforceable against a later sale or a later charge lodges it at the District Lands Office under the Sale of Immovable Property (Specific Performance) Law. The period practitioners work to is six months from signing. Confirm the current deadline with the lawyer and with the department, because a late deposit can leave the buyer as an unsecured creditor of the seller. Lodging the contract does not transfer the title. It protects the right to insist on the transfer later.

The Ministry of Interior’s overview of a purchase is [purchasing property](https://www.gov.cy/moi/en/purchasing-property/).

## Who needs permission to buy

Citizens of non-EU countries need permission before the transfer. The Ministry of Interior’s current page says foreign nationals, which it defines as citizens of non-EU states, including companies it treats as foreign-controlled, apply on form COMM 145 at the District Administration where the property is. The ministry says no fee is payable for the permission and that a straightforward file takes about two to three weeks. Cap. 109 says a contract does not give the buyer the right to acquire the property until the permit is granted. Paying a deposit is not the same as owning the flat.

The ministry’s limits, as that page states them, are a plot of up to 4,000 square metres for a dwelling the owner will live in, or up to two units. The units may be two dwellings, or one dwelling and a shop of up to 100 square metres, or one dwelling and an office of up to 250 square metres. A couple shares the limit and receives joint permission. The Greek text of Cap. 109 on CyLaw places EU citizens and EEA citizens outside the definition of alien. An old English consolidation still describes an earlier residence test. Prefer the ministry’s current page and the Greek consolidation. The site’s shorter note on that permission is [buying as a foreigner](/en/buying-property-cyprus-foreigner/).

## Tax and fees that are not the price

The price on the contract is not the cash you need on completion day. Three charges come up in almost every purchase. Each one depends on facts this page cannot see.

| Charge | When it comes up | Where to confirm it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VAT | Usually on a new property, a first supply by a developer | Tax Department. A reduced rate for a first home has conditions |
| Transfer fees | When the title is transferred at the Land Registry | Department of Lands and Surveys. PwC’s 2026 booklet states a scale; the receipt is the department’s |
| Stamp duty | On the contract, if the instrument still attracts it after the 2026 reform | Tax Department |

PwC’s Tax Facts and Figures 2026 states transfer fees of 3 percent on the first €85,000, 5 percent from €85,001 to €170,000 and 8 percent above that, then says no transfer fee is payable if VAT applies, and that the fees are reduced by 50 percent if VAT does not apply. Those sentences are in a booklet. The Land Registry charges the fee. Run a sketch on the [MyCyTax transfer-fee calculator](https://mycytax.com/calculators/transfer-fees/) and the [VAT calculator](https://mycytax.com/calculators/vat/), then confirm both numbers before completion. Standard VAT is 19 percent. A 5 percent rate for a qualifying first home exists, with area and value conditions the Tax Department publishes. This guide does not copy a square-metre cap it has not set beside the current notice.

As of 2026, check the official page. A developer’s “all-in” price that was calculated last spring may use a stamp-duty figure that no longer exists, or a VAT rate the unit does not qualify for.

## The title deed

Title is the Land Registry record after transfer. Until that record names the buyer, the buyer has a contract and, if it was lodged in time, a protected right to insist on transfer. A separate title for an apartment can lag the handover by a long time when the building is new. Ask what is missing if the answer is that a separate title is not issued yet, and do not treat a promised date as a date in the contract unless it is written as one.

On completion the buyer pays the transfer fee the registry assesses, the seller clears the charges the search found, and the registry records the new owner. Only then does the utility transfer and the building’s management fee become a simple change of name. Until then, keep the lodged contract and the receipts.

## After the keys

A purchase does not by itself create tax residence, and it does not by itself create a residence permit. The immigration permit that is tied to a €300,000 investment has its own property rules, set out in [permanent residence](/en/cyprus-permanent-residency-300k/). The running cost of the home is in [the cost of living](/en/cost-of-living-cyprus/). Renting instead is [renting an apartment](/en/renting-apartment-cyprus/).

## Useful services

- A lawyer for the buyer, instructed before the deposit, for the title search and the contract. The Cyprus Bar Association is the place to check that a person is admitted.
- A survey if the building is old or the paperwork is thin. The surveyor’s report is not a title search.
- Buildings insurance from the day the risk passes, which the contract should define. The site’s [health-insurance guide](/en/international-health-insurance/) is about medical cover, not about the building.
- Tax on the purchase, sketched and then checked, on [MyCyTax](https://mycytax.com).

## Property search and a document check

If you want a second pair of eyes on a contract, a title search or a choice between two areas, use the [property consultation](/en/property-consultation/). Say that you want to buy, name the city, and mention whether a title exists. The form asks for a name and an email. It is not a valuation. You can also write to [cynews24@gmail.com](mailto:cynews24@gmail.com).
